messages.subject: writer streams
parts: Under the master branch, exceptions are written to stderr but progress reports are written to stdout. Under the develop branch, it seems like exceptions are written to stdout along with progress reports. Is that intentional?

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] writer streams
parts:
I'll need to double check, but I don't think anything was ever written out to stderr. If it did in the past, then it was an unintended side effect due to not having a handle on all the places where streams were plugged in.

Can you point out where the errors were output to stderr? Do you need that functionality back?



Daniel

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] writer streams
parts:
On Sunday, March 27, 2016 at 11:36:02 PM UTC-4, Daniel Lee wrote:
I'll need to double check, but I don't think anything was ever written out to stderr. If it did in the past, then it was an unintended side effect due to not having a handle on all the places where streams were plugged in.

Can you point out where the errors were output to stderr? Do you need that functionality back?

It may have been an unintentional feature but it was a good feature. With rstan based on master, I could sink(*, output = "messages") and the progress would go to the screen while the exceptions would go to a temporary file. That is why no rstanarm users are complaining about the Informational Messages because we don't show them that file.

Ben
